entities.description: Michelin-recognized Hong Kong dim sum chain now wholly owned by Jollibee Foods Corporation, with multiple branches across Metro Manila.

entities.name: Max's Restaurant
entities.description: Iconic Filipino fried-chicken and Filipino-cuisine restaurant chain and flagship brand of Max's Group, Inc.

entities.name: Pancake House
entities.description: Filipino all-day breakfast and casual dining chain under Max's Group, Inc. (formerly named Pancake House, Inc.).

entities.name: Yellow Cab Pizza
entities.description: New York-style pizza chain founded in the Philippines in 2001, now owned by Max's Group, Inc.

entities.name: Krispy Kreme Philippines
entities.description: American doughnut chain operated in the Philippines under franchise by Max's Group, Inc.

entities.name: Dencio's
entities.description: Filipino casual dining and grill restaurant chain known for pulutan, owned by Max's Group, Inc.

entities.name: Sizzlin' Steak
entities.description: Budget sizzling-steak casual dining chain owned by Max's Group, Inc.

entities.name: Teriyaki Boy
entities.description: Japanese-inspired fast-casual restaurant chain owned by Max's Group, Inc.

entities.name: Jamba Juice Philippines
entities.description: American smoothie and juice chain franchised in the Philippines by Max's Group, Inc.

entities.name: Le Coeur de France
entities.description: French-style bakery-cafe chain owned by Max's Group, Inc.

entities.name: Zark's Burgers
entities.description: Filipino gourmet burger chain founded in Manila in 2009 by Zark Varona, known for its Yolkmageddon burger.

entities.name: Minute Burger
entities.description: Long-running Filipino buy-1-take-1 burger stand brand operating since 1982, owned by Leslie Corporation (maker of Clover Chips) and franchised since 2003.

entities.name: S&R New York Style Pizza
entities.description: New York-style pizza-by-the-slice chain operated as part of Puregold/S&R Membership Shopping under Cosco Capital.

entities.name: Frankie's New York Buffalo Wings
entities.description: Filipino buffalo-wings restaurant chain founded in 2012 by Eduardo Que Firmalo, Kevin Te, and Bin Tañedo, operated by Buffalo Frankie, Inc.

entities.name: Gerry's Grill
entities.description: Filipino casual dining and grill restaurant chain founded in 1997 in Quezon City by Gerardo Apolinario and Jerome Ngo, with over 110 Philippine branches.

entities.name: Army Navy Burger + Burrito
entities.description: Filipino American-inspired burger and burrito chain founded in 2009, with over 60 branches nationwide.

entities.name: Splash Corporation
entities.description: Philippine personal-care manufacturer founded in 1985 by the Hortaleza family, now the country's largest hand-and-body-lotion and local face-care maker; acquired by India's Wipro Enterprises in 2019 and operated as Wipro Consumer Care's Philippine subsidiary.

entities.name: Procter & Gamble Philippines
entities.description: Philippine subsidiary of the U.S. consumer-goods multinational, headquartered in Bonifacio Global City, Taguig, marketing laundry, hair-care, oral-care, shaving, skin-care and baby/feminine-care brands across the country.

entities.name: Colgate-Palmolive Philippines
entities.description: Philippine subsidiary of U.S.-based Colgate-Palmolive Company, distributing oral-care, bar-soap and deodorant brands nationwide.

entities.name: Beiersdorf Philippines
entities.description: Philippine subsidiary of German skin-care group Beiersdorf AG, based in Taguig's Bonifacio Global City, marketing the NIVEA brand locally.

entities.name: Peerless Products Manufacturing Corporation
entities.description: Filipino household- and personal-care manufacturer established in 1963, best known for launching Champion, the country's first major local laundry-detergent bar brand, in 1977; note the similarly named 'Pride' detergent is a separate brand made by ACS Manufacturing Corporation, not Peerless.

entities.name: ACS Manufacturing Corporation
entities.description: Filipino manufacturer of the value-tier Pride laundry detergent brand; frequently and incorrectly assumed to be part of Peerless Products, which makes the similarly positioned Champion brand.

entities.name: Green Cross, Inc.
entities.description: Filipino hygiene-products company and the Philippines' leading rubbing-alcohol brand, also selling hand-sanitizing gels, sanitizer sprays and antibacterial soap under its own Green Cross name.

entities.name: Personal Collection Direct Selling, Inc.
entities.description: Quezon City-based Filipino direct-selling company founded by Willie Evangelista with over 650 branches nationwide, selling cosmetics (including its In The Mood lipstick line), home care and other household products through a reseller network.

entities.name: Watsons Philippines
entities.description: Health-and-beauty retail chain in the Philippines under Hong Kong-based A.S. Watson Group, operating stores and an e-commerce platform selling both third-party and its own private-label personal-care lines.

entities.name: Lux
entities.description: Global beauty-soap and body-wash brand owned by Unilever and distributed in the Philippines by Unilever Philippines.

entities.name: Sunsilk
entities.description: Unilever shampoo and conditioner brand widely sold in the Philippines, positioned against P&G's Pantene and Rejoice in the mass hair-care segment.

entities.name: Rexona
entities.description: Unilever antiperspirant-deodorant brand distributed in the Philippines, a top seller in the local deodorant category.

entities.name: Closeup
entities.description: Unilever gel toothpaste brand sold in the Philippines, marketed around fresh-breath and social-confidence positioning.

entities.name: Eskinol
entities.description: Facial cleanser and toner brand sold in the Philippines since 1945; now owned and marketed by Unilever Philippines under its skin-care portfolio, despite being commonly misremembered as a purely local independent brand.

entities.name: Vaseline
entities.description: Global petroleum-jelly and body-lotion brand owned by Unilever and sold widely in the Philippines.

entities.name: Lifebuoy
entities.description: Unilever antibacterial bar-soap and body-wash brand distributed in the Philippines, positioned on germ protection.

entities.name: Master
entities.description: Unilever Philippines men's face-care brand (facial washes and scrubs) marketed as a pioneer of men's skincare in the country.

entities.name: Surf
entities.description: Unilever laundry-detergent brand (bars, powders and liquids) sold in the Philippine home-care market.

entities.name: Breeze
entities.description: Unilever laundry-detergent brand distributed in the Philippines, competing in the same shelf set as Surf and P&G's Tide and Ariel.

entities.name: Sunlight
entities.description: Unilever dishwashing-liquid brand and one of the most recognized home-care products in Philippine households.

entities.name: Safeguard
entities.description: P&G antibacterial bar-soap brand and a long-time category leader in the Philippines.

entities.name: Olay
entities.description: P&G facial skin-care brand (moisturizers, serums) sold in the Philippines, competing with Unilever's POND'S and Beiersdorf's NIVEA in facial moisturizers.

entities.name: Head & Shoulders
entities.description: P&G anti-dandruff shampoo brand sold in the Philippines.

entities.name: Pantene
entities.description: P&G shampoo and conditioner brand and a leading hair-care line in the Philippines.

entities.name: Rejoice
entities.description: P&G shampoo brand positioned in the value-to-mid hair-care segment in the Philippines.

entities.name: Gillette
entities.description: P&G men's shaving and grooming brand (razors, blades) sold in the Philippines.

entities.name: Old Spice
entities.description: P&G men's deodorant and body-wash brand sold in the Philippines.

entities.name: Downy
entities.description: P&G fabric-conditioner brand, one of the top-selling home-care products in the Philippines.

entities.name: Ariel
entities.description: P&G premium laundry-detergent brand sold in the Philippines, positioned against Unilever's Surf and Breeze.

entities.name: Tide
entities.description: P&G laundry-detergent brand sold in the Philippines.

entities.name: Joy
entities.description: P&G dishwashing-liquid brand sold in the Philippines, competing directly with Unilever's Sunlight.

entities.name: Pampers
entities.description: P&G baby-diaper brand and a leading disposable-diaper line in the Philippine market.

entities.name: Whisper
entities.description: P&G feminine-hygiene (sanitary napkin) brand sold in the Philippines.

entities.name: Oral-B
entities.description: P&G oral-care brand (toothbrushes, toothpaste) distributed in the Philippines.

entities.name: Colgate
entities.description: Colgate-Palmolive's flagship toothpaste and oral-care brand, a long-standing category leader in the Philippines.

entities.name: Palmolive
entities.description: Colgate-Palmolive bar-soap, body-wash and shampoo brand sold in the Philippines.

entities.name: Protex
entities.description: Colgate-Palmolive antibacterial bar-soap brand competing directly with Safeguard and Lifebuoy in the Philippines.

entities.name: Lady Speed Stick
entities.description: Colgate-Palmolive antiperspirant-deodorant brand sold in the Philippines, competing with Unilever's Rexona.

entities.name: SkinWhite
entities.description: Splash Corporation's skin-whitening lotion and soap brand, one of the leading players in the Philippine whitening-skincare category.

entities.name: Maxi-Peel
entities.description: Splash Corporation's exfoliating-lotion brand launched under its Extraderm skincare line in 1991, a long-running leader in the Philippine facial-peel/exfoliant category.

entities.name: Vitress
entities.description: Splash Corporation hair-care brand offering specialized hair treatments and solutions in the Philippines.

entities.name: Kolours
entities.description: Splash Corporation's home hair-coloring brand sold in the Philippines.

entities.name: Hygienix
entities.description: Splash Corporation antibacterial personal-hygiene brand (alcohol and sanitizing products) sold in the Philippines.

entities.name: Champion
entities.description: Peerless Products' flagship laundry-detergent brand, launched in 1977 as one of the first major locally made detergent bars in the Philippines, now spanning powders, liquid fabric conditioners and dishwashing liquids.

entities.name: Calla
entities.description: Peerless Products' fragrance-forward laundry-detergent brand launched in 2012, positioned alongside Champion in the Philippine home-care market.

entities.name: Hana
entities.description: Peerless Products' personal-care brand offering hair shampoo and conditioner in the Philippines.

entities.name: Pride
entities.description: Value-tier Filipino laundry-detergent brand made by ACS Manufacturing Corporation; often mistakenly attributed to Peerless Products because of its similarity in positioning to Peerless's Champion brand.

entities.name: NIVEA
entities.description: German skin-care and body-care brand owned by Beiersdorf, distributed in the Philippines through Beiersdorf Philippines.

entities.name: Watsons Own Brand
entities.description: Watsons Philippines' private-label personal-care and skincare lines (including Cleene, Dermaid, Belfour and Collagen WS) sold exclusively through Watsons stores and its e-shop.

entities.name: Nature Republic Philippines
entities.description: Philippine retail operation of South Korean cosmetics brand Nature Republic, which opened its first PH store in November 2012 and operates multiple mall branches nationwide.

entities.name: Innisfree Philippines
entities.description: Philippine market presence of South Korean skincare brand Innisfree (Amorepacific); after scaling back physical stores, it now sells primarily through Shopee, Lazada and TikTok Shop.

entities.name: The Face Shop Philippines
entities.description: Philippine retail presence of South Korean cosmetics brand The Face Shop (LG Household & Health Care), part of the mid-2010s wave of K-beauty chains entering PH malls.

entities.name: Maybelline
entities.description: Global mass-cosmetics brand that has been owned by L'Oréal since 1996 and is distributed in the Philippines by L'Oréal Philippines, despite widely being assumed to be an independent American company.

entities.name: Snoe Beauty
entities.description: Independent Filipino cosmetics and skincare brand founded in 2010 by Jen Gerodias Diaz, formulated and produced locally, with multiple retail branches nationwide.

entities.name: Luxe Organix
entities.description: Independent Filipino skincare brand operating since 2004 under CEO Eugene Yap, known for affordable natural-leaning skincare sold widely through Watsons and other retailers; not a Watsons private label despite frequently being sold under 'Only at Watsons' promotions.

entities.name: Zenutrients
entities.description: Independent Filipino natural hair- and skin-care brand founded in 2007, known for gugo-based haircare and led by GM Angela Reyes-Dinglasan; not affiliated with Unilever despite her prior marketing career there.

entities.name: Issy & Co.
entities.description: Independent Filipino vegan, cruelty-free cosmetics brand founded in 2019 by Jasmine Ang Chua and creative director Joel Andrade, focused on inclusive shade ranges for a wide spectrum of Filipino skin tones.

entities.name: GRWM Cosmetics
entities.description: Independent Filipino cosmetics brand founded in 2019 by former nurse and beauty content creator Mae Layug-Madriñan, built around shades formulated for morena (deep) skin tones.

entities.name: Ilog Maria
entities.description: Independent Filipino natural personal-care brand based on a honeybee farm in Silang, Cavite, making beeswax- and honey-based soaps, body washes, lip balms and other personal-care products.

entities.name: FS Cosmetics
entities.description: Independent Filipino mass-market cosmetics brand owned by Edmon Ngo's Cosmetics Revelation Corporation, building on his family's earlier pioneering Philippine cosmetics manufacturing business.

entities.name: Flawless Face & Body
entities.description: Philippine aesthetic-clinic and skincare-retail chain founded in 2001 by owner-CEO Rubby Sy, offering facial, body and medical aesthetic services alongside its own skincare product line.

entities.name: The SM Store
entities.description: Full-line department store banner of SM Retail selling apparel, home, beauty and lifestyle goods, anchoring most SM Supermalls nationwide.

entities.name: SM Supermarket
entities.description: Mid-to-upscale grocery banner of SM Retail's SM Markets division, typically anchoring larger SM malls.

entities.name: SM Hypermarket
entities.description: Large-format grocery-and-general-merchandise banner of SM Retail's SM Markets division, combining supermarket and department-store style bulk assortments.

entities.name: Savemore Market
entities.description: Value-format community grocery banner operated by SM Retail's Supervalue Inc. unit, sized for smaller neighborhoods than SM Supermarket.

entities.name: WalterMart
entities.description: Supermarket-and-mall chain founded by the Lim family (Waltermart Group) that entered a 2013 joint venture giving SM Retail a 51% stake while Waltermart continues day-to-day operation of its stores.

entities.name: Alfamart Philippines
entities.description: Neighborhood mini-mart chain launched in 2014 as a joint venture between SM Investments and Indonesia's PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (which holds roughly a 35% stake), passing 2,300+ stores by late 2025.

entities.name: Kultura Filipino
entities.description: SM Retail specialty banner selling Filipino-made handicrafts, home decor, fashion and gifts, positioned to showcase local artisans and designers.

entities.name: Miniso Philippines
entities.description: Philippine franchise of Chinese lifestyle-and-novelty retailer MINISO, brought to the country in 2016 through a local partnership with the SM Group.

entities.name: Our Home
entities.description: SM Retail furniture-and-home-furnishings banner.

entities.name: Toy Kingdom
entities.description: SM Retail toy-and-baby-products banner operating inside SM malls nationwide.

entities.name: Sports Central
entities.description: SM Retail specialty banner selling sporting goods, athletic apparel and footwear.

entities.name: Pet Express
entities.description: Pet-supplies retail chain in which SM Retail holds a minority stake, operating stores inside SM malls.

entities.name: Robinsons Supermarket
entities.description: Full-service grocery banner of Robinsons Retail Holdings' Food Group, typically anchoring Robinsons malls.

entities.name: Robinsons Easymart
entities.description: Smaller-format community grocery banner within Robinsons Retail Holdings' Food Group, sized between a mini-mart and a full supermarket.

entities.name: Uncle John's
entities.description: Philippine convenience-store chain that operated as Ministop from 2000 under a JV between Robinsons and Japan's Ministop Co. (Aeon); Robinsons Retail bought out Ministop's 40% stake in January 2022 and rebranded the fully owned chain as Uncle John's in late 2022, named for founder John Gokongwei Jr.

entities.name: Robinsons Department Store
entities.description: Full-line department store banner of Robinsons Retail Holdings, anchoring Robinsons malls with apparel, home and lifestyle goods.

entities.name: Handyman Do It Best
entities.description: Home-improvement and hardware banner of Robinsons Retail Holdings' DIY division, affiliated with the U.S. Do It Best co-op.

entities.name: True Value Philippines
entities.description: Hardware and home-improvement banner operated under Robinsons Retail Holdings' DIY division as the Philippine franchise of the U.S. True Value co-op.

entities.name: Daiso Japan Philippines
entities.description: Philippine franchise of Japanese variety/novelty retailer Daiso, operated under Robinsons Retail Holdings' Specialty Store division.

entities.name: Southstar Drug
entities.description: One of the Philippines' oldest drugstore chains, founded by the Dy family in the Bicol region roughly 90 years ago and acquired by Robinsons Retail Holdings in 2012.

entities.name: Rose Pharmacy
entities.description: Cebu-based drugstore chain founded by the Lim family in 1952 and acquired by Robinsons Retail Holdings in 2020, giving the group a combined Southstar-Rose network of about 900 stores.

entities.name: The Generics Pharmacy
entities.description: Franchised community-drugstore chain founded by Benjamin Liuson and operated by Robinsons Retail Holdings, the largest chain of generics-focused drugstores in the Philippines with over 2,000 outlets.

entities.name: No Brand Philippines
entities.description: Korean private-label grocery concept from Shinsegae's E-mart, brought to Manila by Robinsons Retail Holdings in November 2019; Robinsons announced in March 2026 it is closing all 11 remaining No Brand PH stores by end-June 2026 as it exits the venture.

entities.name: Robinsons Appliances
entities.description: Consumer-electronics-and-appliance retail banner of Robinsons Retail Holdings' Specialty Store division.

entities.name: Great Deals E-commerce Corp.
entities.description: Robinsons Retail Holdings' e-distribution and e-commerce arm, operating GoRobinsons.ph, which houses Robinsons Supermarket, Robinsons Department Store, Handyman, True Value and other Robinsons banners online.

entities.name: Robinsons Malls
entities.description: Shopping-mall network developed and operated by Robinsons Land Corporation (Gokongwei family/JG Summit), the second-largest mall chain in the Philippines behind SM Supermalls.

entities.name: S&R Membership Shopping
entities.description: U.S.-style membership warehouse-club chain operated by Puregold, offering bulk groceries and imported goods alongside S&R New York Style QSR food outlets.

entities.name: Budgetlane
entities.description: Value-format supermarket banner operated by Puregold, a smaller-store complement to the flagship Puregold banner.

entities.name: NE Bodega
entities.description: Warehouse-style discount supermarket banner operated by Puregold under the Cosco Capital group.

entities.name: Office Warehouse
entities.description: Office-and-school-supplies retail chain operated as part of Cosco Capital's specialty-retailing segment.

entities.name: Philippine Seven Corporation
entities.description: Exclusive Philippine licensee of the 7-Eleven convenience-store brand since 1982, the largest c-store network in the country; majority-owned (about 56.9% as of October 2025) by Taiwan's President Chain Store Corp.

entities.name: FamilyMart Philippines
entities.description: Japanese convenience-store brand that entered the Philippines via a local franchise partnership in the 2010s; its Philippine store network wound down, ceding the segment to 7-Eleven, Ministop/Uncle John's and Alfamart.

entities.name: SSI Group
entities.description: PSE-listed specialty retailer controlled by the Tantoco family (Rustan's), operating roughly 90+ international franchise brands and 550+ stores across fashion, beauty and food, including Zara, Tory Burch, Calvin Klein and (until May 2026) Marks & Spencer.

entities.name: Zara Philippines
entities.description: Philippine franchise of Spanish fast-fashion retailer Zara (Inditex), operated locally by SSI Group.

entities.name: Marks & Spencer Philippines
entities.description: British department-store/food brand franchised in the Philippines by SSI Group for nearly 40 years; SSI announced it is exiting the franchise, with all M&S PH stores closing by May 2026.

entities.name: Golden ABC, Inc.
entities.description: Filipino fashion-retail conglomerate founded in 1986, owner of proprietary casualwear and streetwear brands Penshoppe, Oxgn, ForMe, Memo, Regatta and Bocu, with over 1,000 stores across Southeast Asia.

entities.name: Penshoppe
entities.description: Golden ABC's flagship affordable casual-wear brand and the Philippines' best-known homegrown fast-fashion label, sold across Southeast Asia.

entities.name: Suyen Corporation
entities.description: Fashion-and-lifestyle conglomerate founded in 1987 by Ben Chan, headquartered in Bonifacio Global City; owns homegrown brands Bench, Human and Kashieca and holds local franchise rights to several international labels.

entities.name: Bench
entities.description: Suyen Corporation's flagship Filipino clothing-and-lifestyle brand, covering apparel, underwear, fragrances and accessories, one of the country's best-known homegrown fashion labels.

entities.name: AllValue Holdings Corp.
entities.description: Retail holding company of businessman Manuel B. Villar Jr., headquartered in Las Piñas City, overseeing publicly listed home-improvement chain AllHome and supermarket chain AllDay Marts along with smaller food-and-retail concepts.

entities.name: AllHome
entities.description: PSE-listed home-improvement, furniture and construction-materials retail chain owned by Manuel Villar's AllValue Holdings, competing directly with Wilcon Depot and CW Home Depot.

entities.name: AllDay Marts
entities.description: PSE-listed supermarket chain (with in-store and online grocery) owned by Manuel Villar's AllValue Holdings, positioned as a newer challenger to Puregold, SM and Robinsons in Philippine grocery retail.

entities.name: CW Home Depot
entities.description: Cebu-founded home-improvement and construction-supplies retail chain operated by CW Marketing & Development Corporation, a joint venture involving Cebu Oversea Hardware Company; unrelated to the U.S. Home Depot chain.

entities.name: Abenson
entities.description: Family-owned appliance-and-gadget retail chain founded by Wilson Lim, operating in the Philippines since 1970 and now the country's largest appliance-and-gadget retailer with over 120 stores.

entities.name: Anson's
entities.description: Long-running Manila-based department store and appliance retailer (Anson Emporium Corporation).

entities.name: Western Appliances
entities.description: Appliance and home-electronics retail chain operating in Metro Manila since 1965.

entities.name: Automatic Centre
entities.description: One of the Philippines' oldest appliance retailers, started in 1948 by Benito Lim, whose sons later founded Abenson and Blim's Fine Furniture.

entities.name: MerryMart
entities.description: Grocery-retail chain launched in 2019 by Mang Inasal founder Edgar "Injap" Sia II through his holding firm Injap Investments, targeting rapid nationwide expansion of grocery centers.

entities.name: Mercury Drug
entities.description: The Philippines' largest drugstore chain, founded in 1945 by Mariano Que and still privately held and led by the Que family (chair Vivian Que-Azcona); operates 450+ company-owned and franchised stores and is estimated to sell roughly 60% of all medicines sold annually in the country.

entities.name: Zalora Philippines
entities.description: Online fashion-and-beauty marketplace operating in the Philippines since 2012 as part of Berlin-based Global Fashion Group, processing over a million orders a month locally.

entities.name: Carousell Philippines
entities.description: Consumer-to-consumer online classifieds/marketplace app in the Philippines, tracing back to AyosDito.ph and Telenor-owned 701Search before Carousell's 2019 merger with 701Search brought the local operation under the Carousell Group.

entities.name: Grab Philippines
entities.description: Philippine operations of Southeast Asian super-app Grab Holdings (Nasdaq: GRAB), running the GrabFood food-delivery and GrabMart quick-commerce/grocery-delivery services alongside ride-hailing and GCash-rival GrabPay.

entities.name: foodpanda Philippines
entities.description: Food-and-grocery delivery platform in the Philippines owned by Germany's Delivery Hero SE; alongside GrabFood it accounts for the large majority of the local food-delivery market (about 39% share in 2024, versus Grab's 61%).

entities.name: edamama
entities.description: Filipino digital platform for parents launched in May 2020, combining e-commerce, content and community around baby and mother-care products, and later expanding into permanent physical stores and its own 'bean' brand.

entities.name: AB Leisure Exponent, Inc.
entities.description: Wholly owned subsidiary of DigiPlus Interactive Corp. that has operated the Bingo Bonanza land-based bingo brand and a network of 130+ bingo parlors nationwide since 1995, and helped launch the BingoPlus digital platform in 2022.

entities.name: Total Gamezone Xtreme, Inc. (GameZone)
entities.description: Wholly owned subsidiary of DigiPlus Interactive Corp. operating PAGCOR e-Games stations and the GameZone/SpinPlus digital slots and e-casino brands.

entities.name: DFNN, Inc.
entities.description: PSE-listed technology company whose subsidiaries and affiliates hold PAGCOR licenses for electronic gaming machines, a sports-betting exchange, and digital pari-mutuel games under its Fun and Games e-bingo/e-games brand.

entities.name: Pacific Online Systems Corporation
entities.description: PSE-listed (Pasig-based) lottery technology company that designs, leases, and manages online lottery terminals and systems for PCSO, operating through subsidiaries including Total Gaming Technologies and Loto Pacific Leisure.

entities.name: Total Gaming Technologies, Inc.
entities.description: Subsidiary of Pacific Online Systems Corporation supporting lottery terminal operations and systems for the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office lottery network.

entities.name: Orient Capital Ventures, Inc.
entities.description: Operator (under the AsianLogic group) of the MegaSportsWorld retail and online sports-betting brand and a PAGCOR-registered e-bingo/e-games service provider.

entities.name: MegaSportsWorld
entities.description: PAGCOR-licensed sports-betting brand (operated by Orient Capital Ventures) running retail betting outlets since 2007 and, since a 2021 PAGCOR approval, an online PIGO sportsbook platform.

entities.name: PAGCOR e-Games
entities.description: PAGCOR's own e-Games/e-Bingo program, under which the agency licenses and directly operates or franchises electronic gaming/bingo stations nationwide through accredited service providers.

entities.name: Newport World Resorts
entities.description: Integrated resort and casino near NAIA in Pasay, developed and operated by Travellers International Hotel Group (Alliance Global Group); originally launched in 2009 as Resorts World Manila with Genting Hong Kong as a 40% partner until Alliance Global completed a full buyout in July 2026.

entities.name: Hann Casino Resort
entities.description: PAGCOR-licensed integrated casino resort in Clark Freeport Zone, Pampanga (rebranded from Widus Hotel & Casino), operated by Hann Philippines and linked to South Korean businessman Dae Sik Han.

entities.name: Fontana Leisure Parks and Casino
entities.description: PAGCOR-licensed casino and leisure park resort in Clark Freeport Zone, Pampanga, one of the region's longer-standing regional casino operators.

entities.name: Midori Clark Hotel and Casino
entities.description: PAGCOR-licensed hotel-casino in Clark Freeport Zone, Pampanga, catering primarily to a regional/East Asian gaming clientele.

entities.name: Royce Hotel and Casino
entities.description: PAGCOR-licensed hotel-casino in Clark Freeport Zone, Pampanga, one of the cluster of regional casino resorts serving Central Luzon.

entities.name: NUSTAR Resort & Casino
entities.description: Five-star integrated resort and casino on Cebu City's South Road Properties, developed by Universal Hotels & Resorts and holding a PAGCOR gaming license; opened May 2022 as the first upscale integrated resort outside Metro Manila/Clark.

entities.name: JPark Island Resort & Waterpark
entities.description: Large family resort and waterpark in Mactan, Cebu, that also hosts a regional PAGCOR-licensed gaming/casino facility on-site; gaming scale is modest relative to Entertainment City or Clark IRs.

entities.name: Winford Manila Resort and Casino
entities.description: PAGCOR-licensed hotel-casino in Sta. Cruz, Manila, historically also serving as a retail outlet location for third-party sports-betting operators such as MegaSportsWorld.

entities.name: Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office
entities.description: Government-owned corporation that operates the national and provincial lottery draws (Lotto, Small Town Lottery), sweepstakes, and keno, using revenue to fund health and charity programs, and contracts private firms for lottery systems and terminals.

entities.name: Philippine Gaming Management Corporation
entities.description: Lottery systems and equipment provider (part of Malaysia's Berjaya Group) that, in a 2021 joint venture with Pacific Online Systems and International Lottery & Totalizator Systems, won PCSO's five-year automated lottery system contract worth roughly PHP5.8 billion.

entities.name: Casino Filipino
entities.description: Chain of casinos directly operated by PAGCOR across the Philippines; PAGCOR has for years pursued a 'decoupling'/privatization plan to sell off Casino Filipino branches and become a pure regulator, most recently targeting completion by around 2027.

entities.name: Cagayan Economic Zone Authority
entities.description: Economic zone authority (established 1995) for the Cagayan Special Economic Zone and Freeport in Santa Ana, Cagayan, which since 2001 has authorized offshore/interactive online gaming licenses through appointed master licensors.

entities.name: First Cagayan Leisure and Resort Corporation
entities.description: Private corporation appointed by CEZA (since 2000) as a Master Licensor screening and licensing operators for internet/interactive gaming within the Cagayan Special Economic Zone, mostly serving offshore markets.

entities.name: North Cagayan Gaming and Amusement Corporation
entities.description: Second CEZA-appointed Master Licensee (alongside First Cagayan) managing and overseeing interactive/offshore gaming licenses issued within the Cagayan Special Economic Zone.

entities.name: Aurora Pacific Economic Zone and Freeport Authority
entities.description: Economic zone authority for the Aurora Pacific Economic Zone in Casiguran, Aurora, established under RA 9490; its role in gaming/offshore licensing (analogous to CEZA) is not consistently confirmed and should be treated as unverified.

entities.name: Games and Amusements Board
entities.description: Government regulatory body (created 1951) overseeing professional sports and allied amusement activities in the Philippines, including boxing licensing and (per its charter) organized gambling connected to play-for-pay sports and cockfighting.

entities.name: E-Sabong (Online Cockfighting)
entities.description: Online/live-streamed cockfighting wagering vertical that PAGCOR briefly licensed starting 2021; suspended by President Duterte in May 2022 and formally banned nationwide by President Marcos via Executive Order No. 9 (December 2022), with illegal platforms still being taken down as of 2025-2026.

entities.name: POGO (Philippine Offshore Gaming Operators)
entities.description: Category of online gambling operators licensed by PAGCOR (and offshore-gaming licensees under CEZA/APECO-type authorities) to serve players outside the Philippines; ordered banned nationwide by President Marcos with a phase-out targeted around end of 2024, a directive whose full enforcement status should be independently reconfirmed.

entities.name: Mineski Global
entities.description: Philippine esports pioneer founded in 2004 as a Dota team and incorporated in 2009, now a regional group spanning event production (Mineski Events Team), cyber-cafe franchising (Mineski Infinity), academy/scouting and its Riot Games-appointed Valorant esports agency mandate for the Philippines.

entities.name: Mineski Infinity
entities.description: Mineski Global's gaming-cafe and franchise brand, launched in 2008 as the Philippines' first gamer-focused internet cafe and grown into a nationwide (and regional) franchise network.

entities.name: PlayBook Esports
entities.description: Manila-founded (2015) Philippine esports organization that grew out of the Playbook Videogame & Bookshop retail franchise, specializing in fighting games and NBA 2K and cited alongside Mineski as a founding member of the Philippine Esports Organization ecosystem.

entities.name: Omega Esports
entities.description: Philippine multi-title esports organization launched in February 2019 from a partnership between PLDT/Smart Communications and the Sterling Global Dragons roster, fielding its flagship MLBB team under the sponsor-branded name Smart Omega.

entities.name: The Nationals
entities.description: The Philippines' first franchise-based multi-title esports league, launched in 2019 to build a national-team athlete pipeline under ESNAP sanctioning, which ceased operations in 2022.

entities.name: Liyab Esports
entities.description: Filipino League of Legends/Wild Rift organization powered by Globe Telecom and Mineski that won the 2019 SEA Invitational before disbanding in January 2022 when it sold its LoL PCS franchise slot to Deep Cross Gaming.

entities.name: NAVI PH
entities.description: Philippine women's Mobile Legends division of Ukrainian esports organization Natus Vincere (NAVI), formed in 2025 when NAVI acquired the all-Filipina Smart Omega Empress roster shortly after the team's Esports World Cup 2024 title.

entities.name: RSG Philippines
entities.description: Philippine Mobile Legends division of Singapore-based RSG that joined MPL Philippines in 2021 and won the Season 9 title over Omega Esports, before RSG disbanded all of its MLBB rosters (PH, Singapore, Malaysia) in January 2025.

entities.name: AP.Bren
entities.description: Philippine multi-title esports organization founded in 2017 as Bren Esports, MPL Philippines' first-ever champion, which rebranded to AP.Bren after partnering with AP Esports and went on to win the M2 and M5 Mobile Legends world championships.

entities.name: Team Liquid PH
entities.description: MPL Philippines MLBB franchise with lineage running from AURA Philippines to ECHO Philippines before global esports organization Team Liquid acquired the roster in May 2024, rebranding it Team Liquid PH and winning the MSC 2025 title.

entities.name: Team Falcons PH
entities.description: Philippine MLBB division of Saudi-backed global esports organization Team Falcons, founded in 2025 by acquiring Blacklist International's MPL Philippines slot after an earlier 2024 co-branding tie-up with AP.Bren; runner-up in MPL PH Season 17.

entities.name: Aurora Gaming PH
entities.description: Philippine Mobile Legends division of Serbian esports organization Aurora Gaming, entering MPL Philippines in mid-2024 and quickly becoming a top contender with multiple grand-final runner-up finishes and a record MLBB world-championship viewership peak.

entities.name: Twisted Minds PH
entities.description: Philippine MLBB franchise of Saudi Arabian esports organization Twisted Minds, which entered MPL Philippines alongside fellow Saudi-backed org Team Falcons as Gulf-region investment expanded into the league.

entities.name: Execration
entities.description: Philippine Dota 2 organization founded in 2014, a mainstay of the country's international Dota scene and a former MPL Philippines competitor that departed the league after Season 7.

entities.name: Cignal Ultra
entities.description: Defunct Mobile Legends team fielded by satellite-TV operator Cignal TV during MPL Philippines' pre-franchise era, one of the league's earliest media-company-backed rosters.

entities.name: Level Up! Games
entities.description: Pioneering Philippine online-game publisher founded in 2002 (merged with E-Games in 2012) that once operated Ragnarok Online and other MMOs locally before Thailand's Asiasoft bought it in 2014 and later divested it in 2017.

entities.name: PlayPark
entities.description: Philippine online-game portal operator publishing titles like Ragnarok Online, Cabal and RF Online under Thailand-based Asiasoft/Asphere Innovations, run locally by Hubvantage Services.

entities.name: PlayStation Philippines
entities.description: Sony Interactive Entertainment's PlayStation console/accessory business in the Philippines, distributed since November 2022 through sole local partner Acer Global Merchandise Philippines.

entities.name: Nintendo Philippines
entities.description: Nintendo's Philippine console/software distribution, handled since November 2023 by official distributor VSTECS Phils., with regional distributor Maxsoft (M.M. Soft) later opening the country's first Nintendo Authorized Store in 2026.

entities.name: PUBG Mobile
entities.description: Battle-royale mobile title co-developed by Korea's Krafton and Tencent's Lightspeed Studios, published worldwide including the Philippines under Tencent's Level Infinite games label and a perennial rival to Garena's Free Fire for PH battle-royale mindshare.

entities.name: HoYoverse
entities.description: Shanghai-based developer/publisher of Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero, whose gacha-RPG titles compete for Filipino mobile gamers' time and wallet share against MOBA and battle-royale incumbents.

entities.name: Electronic Arts
entities.description: US AAA game publisher (EA Sports FC, Apex Legends) with a large but mostly digital-distribution presence in the Philippines and no dedicated local publishing office.

entities.name: Ubisoft
entities.description: French AAA game publisher (Assassin's Creed, Rainbow Six) sold in the Philippines mainly through digital storefronts and retail distributors rather than a local subsidiary.

entities.name: Kumu
entities.description: Filipino livestreaming and social-commerce super-app launched in 2018, hosting gaming, variety and shopping livestreams and having raised over US$100 million by 2021 including a General Atlantic-led round.

entities.name: Nimo TV
entities.description: International game-streaming brand of Tencent-backed Huya, used for MLBB and Free Fire livestreams across Southeast Asia including the Philippines.

entities.name: Facebook Gaming
entities.description: Meta's in-app game livestreaming service, launched in 2018, that became especially popular in the Philippines and produced homegrown gaming celebrities like ChooxTV.

entities.name: YouTube Gaming
entities.description: Google's gaming vertical on YouTube, a leading destination for Filipino MLBB/Free Fire livestreams, VODs and esports broadcast simulcasts.

entities.name: Twitch
entities.description: Amazon-owned livestreaming platform with a smaller but growing Filipino gaming-creator base relative to Facebook Gaming and YouTube in the local market.

entities.name: Nonolive
entities.description: Southeast Asian live-social streaming app that gained traction among Filipino and regional gaming/variety streamers in the late 2010s alongside Bigo Live; unverified whether it remains active in the PH market.

entities.name: Acer Predator
entities.description: Acer's gaming hardware line (laptops, monitors, peripherals) and PredatorGG esports/community program, active as a jersey and hardware sponsor of Philippine teams including Blacklist International; Acer's local unit also distributes PlayStation in the PH.

entities.name: ASUS ROG Philippines
entities.description: Philippine arm of ASUS's Republic of Gamers gaming-hardware brand, sponsoring local gaming cafes, LAN events and content creators alongside its laptop/monitor/peripheral retail business.

entities.name: Logitech Philippines
entities.description: Philippine distribution and marketing arm of Swiss peripherals maker Logitech's gaming sub-brand Logitech G, a common peripheral sponsor across local esports teams and content creators.

entities.name: Oppo Philippines
entities.description: Philippine unit of Chinese smartphone maker Oppo, a mobile-gaming-focused device sponsor of local esports orgs such as Blacklist International.

entities.name: Land Bank of the Philippines
entities.description: Philippine government-owned universal bank founded in 1963, the country's second-largest bank by assets and wholly-owning parent of digital-only Overseas Filipino Bank.

entities.name: Overseas Filipino Bank
entities.description: Wholly government-owned, branchless digital-only bank converted from the former Philippine Postal Savings Bank in 2018 to serve overseas Filipino workers, and the first entity to receive a BSP digital-bank license.

entities.name: Security Bank Corporation
entities.description: Independently held, Filipino-controlled universal bank listed on the PSE since 1995 and one of the country's largest private banks by assets.

entities.name: Rizal Commercial Banking Corporation
entities.description: Universal bank majority-owned by the Yuchengco Group of Companies, listed on the PSE, and a bank partner for open-finance API initiatives with fintech Brankas.

entities.name: EastWest Bank
entities.description: Universal bank roughly 60-percent owned by the Gotianun family's Filinvest Development Corporation and listed on the PSE under the ticker EW.

entities.name: Asia United Bank
entities.description: Philippine universal bank founded in 1997 by Jacinto Ng, listed on the PSE and headquartered in Ortigas Center, Pasig.

entities.name: Philippine Savings Bank
entities.description: Thrift-bank subsidiary of Metrobank, listed on the PSE and focused on consumer and SME banking.

entities.name: Robinsons Bank Corporation
entities.description: Formerly Gokongwei-family-owned universal bank that merged into BPI effective January 1, 2024, with its roughly 162 branches absorbed into BPI's network and JG Summit/Robinsons Retail receiving a combined equity stake in BPI.

entities.name: GrabPay
entities.description: E-money wallet embedded in the Grab super-app, BSP-licensed as an electronic money issuer in the Philippines since 2018 and owned by Singapore-based Grab Holdings.

entities.name: Grab Holdings Limited
entities.description: Nasdaq-listed, Singapore-headquartered super-app operator for ride-hailing, delivery and payments across Southeast Asia, and parent of the Philippines' GrabPay e-wallet.

entities.name: Coins.ph
entities.description: Philippine crypto-and-e-wallet 'super app' launched in 2014, holding both BSP Virtual Currency and Electronic Money Issuer licenses, majority-acquired in 2022 by former Binance CFO Wei Zhou from Indonesia's Gojek/GoTo.

entities.name: Dragonpay
entities.description: Philippine online payment gateway founded in 2010 that pioneered over-the-counter/alternative payment collection for e-commerce merchants, and became part of Indonesian payments company Xendit via a 2021 strategic investment.

entities.name: UBX Philippines
entities.description: Fintech and venture-building subsidiary wholly owned by UnionBank of the Philippines, operating the Bux payment-gateway platform and an open-finance API business, and an early institutional investor in crypto exchange PDAX.

entities.name: Brankas
entities.description: Open-finance and banking-as-a-service API provider founded in 2016 and headquartered in Singapore, with a Philippine office in Bonifacio Global City partnering with banks such as RCBC on account-linking and payment-initiation services.

entities.name: Cebuana Lhuillier
entities.description: The Philippines' largest microfinancial-services network and flagship brand of the PJ Lhuillier Group, offering pawnbroking, domestic and international remittance (including a Western Union network tie-up), micro-insurance and bills payment.

entities.name: M Lhuillier Financial Services
entities.description: Cebu City-headquartered pawnshop and remittance chain founded in 1992 by Michel Lhuillier, operating over 3,000 branches nationwide and a longtime rival of Makati-based Cebuana Lhuillier.

entities.name: Palawan Pawnshop
entities.description: Puerto Princesa-founded pawnshop and remittance network built by Bobby and Angelita Castro since 1985, now spanning the Palawan Express Pera Padala remittance service, Palawan Credit and the PalawanPay e-wallet.

entities.name: Western Union
entities.description: US-based global money-transfer company that reaches the Philippines mainly through local agent partners such as Cebuana Lhuillier, serving one of the world's largest remittance-receiving markets.

entities.name: RD Pawnshop
entities.description: Long-running Filipino pawnshop and OTC remittance chain competing with Cebuana Lhuillier, M Lhuillier and Palawan Pawnshop in the pawn-broking segment; detailed ownership records are not independently confirmed.

entities.name: Villarica Pawnshop
entities.description: One of the Philippines' oldest pawnshop chains, competing with Cebuana Lhuillier, M Lhuillier, Palawan Pawnshop and RD Pawnshop in pawn-broking and remittance services; detailed ownership records are not independently confirmed.

entities.name: Home Credit Philippines
entities.description: Consumer-finance and installment-lending provider offering point-of-sale device and appliance loans, historically backed by PPF Group's Home Credit and reported in 2025 to have Thailand's Bank of Ayudhya (Krungsri, part of Japan's MUFG) and Security Bank among its shareholders following a regional restructuring.

entities.name: BillEase
entities.description: Buy-now-pay-later platform operated by First Digital Finance Corporation since 2017, dual-regulated as a financing company by the SEC and as a payment system operator by the BSP.

entities.name: Cashalo
entities.description: Digital consumer-lending app operated by SEC-registered financing company Paloo Financing, Inc.; originally incubated by Hong Kong-based Oriente and now described on its own site as a Tilt venture.

entities.name: Atome Philippines
entities.description: Buy-now-pay-later app operated locally by Neuroncredit Financing Company Inc. under Singapore-based Advance Intelligence Group's regional Atome brand, also offering an Atome Cash personal loan and a savings account.

entities.name: Plentina
entities.description: Manila-based alternative-credit-scoring and buy-now-pay-later fintech that partners with sari-sari stores and retailers to extend microloans to underbanked Filipino consumers.

entities.name: Tala
entities.description: US-founded, AI-driven mobile lending app operating in the Philippines since 2017 alongside Kenya, India, Mexico and other emerging markets, extending small unsecured loans to underserved borrowers using alternative credit data.

entities.name: UnaCash
entities.description: SEC-registered Philippine online lending app offering short-term unsecured cash loans through a mobile-first application process; corporate parent details are not independently confirmed.

entities.name: Digido
entities.description: Online lending app in the Philippines offering short-term installment cash loans, operating under a Digido brand that also appears in other emerging lending markets; corporate parent details are not independently confirmed.

entities.name: JuanHand
entities.description: SEC-registered digital lending app operated by Wefund Lending Corp. out of Quezon City, offering loans up to PHP 50,000 with fast approval and repayment via e-wallets and partner banks.

entities.name: PDAX
entities.description: BSP-licensed Philippine cryptocurrency exchange founded by Nichel Gaba, backed by investors including UnionBank's UBX and Tiger Global, and one of the country's first BSP-licensed virtual asset service providers.

entities.name: Binance
entities.description: World's largest crypto exchange, which does not hold a Philippine license; the SEC issued advisories against it and, with Google and Apple's cooperation, restricted local app-store access starting March 2024 over unregistered securities-like offerings.

entities.name: Bloom Solutions
entities.description: Manila-based, Y Combinator-backed B2B fintech that provides payroll and earned-wage-access/loan-disbursement API infrastructure for employers and lenders in the Philippines.

entities.name: Sun Life Philippines
entities.description: Philippine life-insurance and asset-management arm of Canada's Sun Life Financial, one of the country's largest life insurers by premium income.

entities.name: Pru Life UK
aliases: Pru Life Insurance Corporation of U.K.
entities.description: Philippine life-insurance subsidiary of UK-based Prudential plc, offering protection, health and PRULink investment-linked products.

entities.name: AXA Philippines
entities.description: Life and non-life insurer operating as a joint venture among France's AXA Group, Ayala Corporation and Metrobank Card Corporation, evolved from the legacy Charter Ping An Insurance business.

entities.name: Insular Life
aliases: The Insular Life Assurance Company, Ltd.
entities.description: The Philippines' oldest and largest Filipino-owned life insurer, a mutual (policyholder-owned) company founded in 1910 and headquartered in Alabang, Muntinlupa.

entities.name: Manulife Philippines
aliases: The Manufacturers Life Insurance Co. (Phils.), Inc.
entities.description: Philippine life-insurance subsidiary of Canada's Manulife Financial Corporation, offering protection, health and wealth-accumulation products.

entities.name: Singlife Philippines
entities.description: Mobile-first, app-based life and health insurer operating in the Philippines under Singapore's Singapore Life Pte Ltd, competing on paperless digital policy issuance.

entities.name: FWD Philippines
entities.description: Philippine life insurer under Richard Li's Pacific Century Group-backed FWD Group, known for app-based, direct-to-consumer distribution.

entities.name: BPI AIA Life Assurance Corporation
entities.description: Bancassurance joint venture between BPI and Hong Kong-listed AIA Group, distributing life-insurance and investment-linked products through BPI's branch network, successor to the earlier BPI-Philam tie-up after AIA's 2012 acquisition of Philam Life.

entities.name: Malayan Insurance
entities.description: The Philippines' largest non-life insurer, part of the Yuchengco Group of Companies alongside RCBC.

entities.name: Yuchengco Group of Companies
entities.description: Diversified Filipino conglomerate founded by Alfonso Yuchengco spanning banking (RCBC), non-life insurance (Malayan Insurance), education and automotive distribution.

entities.name: Filinvest Development Corporation
entities.description: Gotianun-family holding company listed on the PSE that controls EastWest Bank alongside real estate, hospitality and power businesses.

entities.name: DITO Telecommunity Corp.
entities.description: The Philippines' third major mobile network operator, launched commercially in 2021 and operated under DITO CME Holdings Corp.

entities.name: PLDT Home
entities.description: PLDT's retail fixed-line broadband, fiber, and IPTV brand for Filipino households.

entities.name: TNT (Talk 'N Text)
entities.description: Smart Communications' value/prepaid mobile brand targeting the budget-conscious segment.

entities.name: Sun Cellular
entities.description: Former Digitel mobile brand absorbed by Smart Communications after the 2011 acquisition; discontinued/merged into Smart's other brands by 2022.

entities.name: GOMO
entities.description: Globe Telecom's fully-digital, app-based prepaid mobile brand launched in October 2020.

entities.name: TM (Touch Mobile)
entities.description: Globe Telecom's budget prepaid mobile brand, with subscriber base transferred to Globe in 2008.

entities.name: Starlink Philippines
entities.description: SpaceX's satellite internet service, commercially available in the Philippines since February 2023 as its first Asian market deployment.

entities.name: Sky Cable Corporation
entities.description: Cable TV and broadband provider held via Sky Vision Corporation (78% Lopez Inc., 18.8% ABS-CBN); a 2023 PLDT acquisition deal for its broadband unit was called off in February 2024.

entities.name: ABS-CBN Corporation
entities.description: Philippine media and entertainment conglomerate controlled by the Lopez family; lost its free-TV broadcast franchise in 2020 and now focuses on content production, cable, and streaming.

entities.name: GMA Network, Inc.
entities.description: Free-to-air broadcast network jointly controlled by the Gozon, Duavit, and Jimenez families through several holding entities.

entities.name: TV5 Network, Inc.
entities.description: Free-to-air broadcast network owned by MediaQuest Holdings (PLDT/MVP group), chaired by Manuel V. Pangilinan since its 2010 acquisition.

entities.name: MediaQuest Holdings, Inc.
entities.description: PLDT's media holding arm, held via the PLDT Beneficial Trust Fund to satisfy constitutional Filipino-ownership rules on mass media; owns TV5, Cignal TV, News5, and stakes in The Philippine Star and BusinessWorld.

entities.name: News5
entities.description: TV5 Network's news division producing news and current-affairs programming under the MediaQuest/PLDT group.

entities.name: CNN Philippines
entities.description: News channel operated by Nine Media Corp. under a Warner Bros. Discovery brand license; ceased operations on January 31, 2024 due to financial losses.

entities.name: Nine Media Corporation
entities.description: Broadcast company that operated CNN Philippines until its 2024 shutdown, and now co-runs RPTV, a joint venture with TV5 launched February 1, 2024.

entities.name: Manila Bulletin
entities.description: Broadsheet newspaper founded in 1900, controlled by the Yap family since the 1980s after Emilio Yap became chairman.

entities.name: Philippine Daily Inquirer
entities.description: Leading broadsheet newspaper; majority (85%) personally owned by San Miguel Corporation president Ramon S. Ang since 2017, with the remainder held by Manuel V. Pangilinan, and restructured as Inquirer Interactive, Inc. in July 2025.

entities.name: The Philippine Star
entities.description: Broadsheet newspaper 51%-owned by PLDT/MediaQuest's Hastings Holdings, alongside legacy Belmonte-family shareholders.

entities.name: Rappler
entities.description: Digital news outlet co-founded by Maria Ressa; the SEC's 2018 revocation of its incorporation was overturned by the Court of Appeals, with its license restored in August 2024.

entities.name: Summit Media
entities.description: Magazine and digital lifestyle publisher (Preview, Cosmopolitan PH, Spot.ph, and others) co-founded by Lisa Gokongwei-Cheng; independently run and not a formal JG Summit subsidiary.

entities.name: Viva Communications, Inc.
entities.description: Film, TV, and music production company chaired by Vic del Rosario Jr.; parent of Viva Films, Viva Records, and the VMX/Vivamax streaming platform.

entities.name: Brightlight Productions
entities.description: ABS-CBN content studio launched in 2021 to produce programming for third-party platforms and networks.

entities.name: Star Magic
entities.description: ABS-CBN's talent management and artist development agency.

entities.name: Kapamilya Channel
entities.description: ABS-CBN's flagship cable/satellite channel distributed via Sky Cable, Cignal, and other pay-TV platforms since losing its free-TV franchise in 2020.

entities.name: iWantTFC
entities.description: ABS-CBN's OTT streaming platform for local and diaspora audiences, combining iWant and The Filipino Channel (TFC) offerings.

entities.name: VMX (formerly Vivamax)
entities.description: Viva Communications' streaming service launched as Vivamax in January 2021 and rebranded VMX in October 2024, known for adult-oriented Filipino originals.

entities.name: GMA Play
entities.description: GMA Network's Philippines-only streaming app for its shows, news, and archive content.

entities.name: Netflix Philippines
entities.description: US-based global SVOD platform's Philippine market presence, a major competitor across local free-TV, cable, and OTT services.

entities.name: Disney+ Philippines
entities.description: The Walt Disney Company's streaming service; standalone Disney+ availability in the Philippines has been limited/recent (e.g., NBA streaming tie-in from November 2025), distinct from the earlier discontinued DisneyLife app.

entities.name: Amazon Prime Video Philippines
entities.description: Amazon's SVOD platform, accessible in the Philippines as part of global Prime Video expansion.

entities.name: Viu Philippines
entities.description: PCCW-owned Hong Kong streaming platform popular in the Philippines for Korean and Asian drama content.

entities.name: iQIYI Philippines
entities.description: Chinese SVOD platform (Baidu-affiliated) with a Philippine app presence, frequently bundled in telco promos.

entities.name: WeTV Philippines
entities.description: Tencent Video's international streaming brand with a Philippine audience for Chinese, Thai, and Filipino content.

entities.name: Spotify Philippines
entities.description: Swedish-founded audio streaming platform competing for Filipino consumers' subscription and attention spend alongside video OTT services.

entities.name: Villar Group of Companies
entities.description: Diversified conglomerate controlled by the Manuel B. Villar Jr. family, spanning residential real estate, malls, retail, and memorial parks.

entities.name: Vista Land & Lifescapes, Inc.
entities.description: The Villar family's flagship publicly-listed homebuilder, the largest integrated property developer in the Philippines by residential land bank.

entities.name: Golden MV Holdings, Inc.
entities.description: Villar family land-banking vehicle associated with large-scale projects such as Villar City.

entities.name: Camella
entities.description: Vista Land's flagship mass-housing subdivision brand and the company's oldest and best-known label.

entities.name: Vistamalls, Inc.
entities.description: Vista Land's mall-operating subsidiary running the Vista Mall and Starmalls shopping-center chains.

entities.name: Prime Asset Ventures, Inc.
entities.description: Villar Group investment/asset-holding vehicle; exact scope of current holdings is not fully public.

entities.name: Lopez Holdings Corporation
entities.description: The Lopez family's publicly-listed top holding company, controlling stakes in ABS-CBN and First Philippine Holdings.

entities.name: First Philippine Holdings Corporation
entities.description: Lopez Group holding company focused on power generation, energy, and property, parent of First Gen and Rockwell Land.

entities.name: First Gen Corporation
entities.description: First Philippine Holdings' power-generation arm, one of the country's largest producers of natural gas and renewable energy.

entities.name: Energy Development Corporation
entities.description: Geothermal and renewable-energy producer within the Lopez Group/First Philippine Holdings portfolio, delisted from the PSE circa 2019 after a tender offer.

entities.name: Rockwell Land Corporation
entities.description: Upscale property developer within the Lopez Group/First Philippine Holdings, built on the former Meralco thermal plant site in Makati.

entities.name: First Balfour, Inc.
entities.description: Engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) arm within the Lopez Group/First Philippine Holdings network.

entities.name: EEI Corporation
entities.description: Yuchengco Group's construction and engineering services company.

entities.name: House of Investments, Inc.
entities.description: Publicly-listed investment holding arm within the Yuchengco Group of Companies.

entities.name: Mapúa University
entities.description: Engineering-focused university within the Yuchengco Group's education arm.

entities.name: PetroEnergy Resources Corporation
entities.description: Yuchengco Group-affiliated energy and petroleum exploration company.

entities.name: Filinvest Land, Inc.
entities.description: Filinvest's real estate development arm covering residential subdivisions, condominiums, and Filinvest City in Alabang.

entities.name: Chroma Hospitality, Inc.
entities.description: Filinvest's hotel management joint venture with Indonesia's Archipelago International, operating the Crimson and Quest hotel brands.

entities.name: Crimson Hotels & Resorts
entities.description: Filinvest/Chroma Hospitality's upscale hotel brand.

entities.name: Filinvest REIT Corp.
entities.description: Publicly-listed real estate investment trust spun off from Filinvest Land's commercial property portfolio.

entities.name: Empire East Land Holdings, Inc.
entities.description: Megaworld affiliate developing affordable and mid-market residential condominiums.

entities.name: Global-Estate Resorts, Inc.
entities.description: Megaworld affiliate focused on leisure and resort-residential developments.

entities.name: Suntrust Properties, Inc.
entities.description: Megaworld's mass-housing and horizontal residential development brand.

entities.name: DoubleDragon Corporation
entities.description: Property and hospitality conglomerate co-founded in 2012 by Edgar 'Injap' Sia II and Tony Tan Caktiong, listed on the PSE.

entities.name: Hotel101 Global
entities.description: DoubleDragon's condotel hospitality brand expanding into international markets including Japan and Spain.

entities.name: CityMall Commercial Centers, Inc.
entities.description: DoubleDragon's community mall chain targeting provincial and second-tier cities.

entities.name: DDMP REIT, Inc.
entities.description: DoubleDragon's publicly-listed real estate investment trust built around the DD Meridian Park development.

entities.name: AboitizLand, Inc.
entities.description: Real estate development arm of Aboitiz Equity Ventures, building residential and mixed-use townships nationwide.

entities.name: Landco Pacific Corporation
entities.description: Leisure and residential property arm associated with Metro Pacific Investments Corporation.

entities.name: Beacon Electric Asset Holdings, Inc.
entities.description: Joint holding vehicle of Metro Pacific Investments Corporation and PLDT Communications and Energy Ventures used to hold their combined stake in Meralco.

entities.name: Philippine Basketball Association
entities.description: Asia's first pro basketball league; a premier sponsorship and naming-rights platform for Philippine brands.

entities.name: Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League
entities.description: Commercial regional PH basketball league; growing brand-sponsorship platform.

entities.name: PeryaGame
entities.description: DigiPlus Interactive digital brand that digitizes traditional Filipino carnival ("perya") games such as Color Game and Pinoy Drop Ball for PAGCOR-regulated online play.

entities.name: SpinPlus
entities.description: DigiPlus Interactive's dedicated online slot-games platform, positioned alongside BingoPlus, ArenaPlus, GameZone and PeryaGame in the group's digital gaming portfolio.

entities.name: Bingo Gallery, Inc.
entities.description: Wholly-owned bingo-operations subsidiary of DigiPlus Interactive Corp., named alongside AB Leisure Exponent and Total Gamezone Xtreme as part of the group's licensed operating entities.

entities.name: Blue Chip Gaming and Leisure Corporation
entities.description: Gaming and leisure subsidiary of DigiPlus Interactive Corp. (formerly Leisure & Resorts World Corporation); listed among the group's corporate subsidiaries in investor/company-profile disclosures.

entities.name: Diginvest Holdings Inc.
entities.description: DigiPlus Interactive subsidiary used as the corporate vehicle for the group's international expansion, which incorporated DigiPlus Global Pte. Ltd. in Singapore.

entities.name: DigiPlus Global Pte. Ltd.
entities.description: Singapore-incorporated holding entity of DigiPlus Interactive (via subsidiary Diginvest Holdings Inc.), set up as part of DigiPlus's international-expansion corporate structure.
